note: Adapted from Maiti 2006; original in English; in Table 12 the maximum head width row of this species reads '0.66—1.21', whose lower limit 0.66 is smaller than the upper limit of the anterior head width in the same table (0.58—0.69), which is clearly an extraction error, so that row is not recorded; the rest is transcribed.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate head nearly circular, wider than long, fontanelle white, slit-like, almost central; antennae 19-segmented, segment 3 the smallest; postclypeus inflated and divided by a median line; pronotum nearly kidney-shaped, narrower than the head, anterior margin with a median notch, posterior margin weakly concave. Soldier head long oval, distinctly narrowed anteriorly, fontanelle fairly large with a distinct chitinous rim; antennae 14-segmented; labrum tip pointed, with a transparent end and two setae; postmentum broad and long, widest in the anterior third, the widest part almost twice the narrowest part below it.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head yellowish brown, wings long and dark brown; the rest of the body paler. Head and pronotum sparsely hairy, body hairs denser, the whole body hairy (Hill, 1942). Head nearly circular, wider than long, sides weakly convex; fontanelle white, slit-like, almost central; antennae 19-segmented, segment 3 the smallest; compound eyes nearly circular, fairly large; ocelli nearly oval; postclypeus inflated and divided by a median line; labrum apical margin nearly rounded. Pronotum nearly kidney-shaped, narrower than the head, anterior margin with a median notch, posterior margin weakly concave. Measurements (mm): body length with wings 11.00—13.00; body length without wings 4.50—7.00; head length to the lateral base of the mandible 0.91—1.06; head width including the eyes 1.00—1.28; maximum eye diameter 0.27—0.40; maximum ocellus diameter 0.12—0.18; pronotum length 0.62—0.70, width 0.91—1.13; forewing length 9.00—10.30; antennae 17—20-segmented.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellowish brown, the rest paler. Head with a few erect hairs; pronotum and abdomen with more hairs. Head long oval, distinctly narrowed anteriorly, fontanelle fairly large with a distinct chitinous rim; antennae 14-segmented (sometimes 13—14), segment 3 and segment 4 nearly equal or variable; labrum tip pointed, with a transparent end and two setae; mandibles slightly straight, the tips weakly incurved. Postmentum broad and long, with a few short hairs on the body, especially anteriorly, widest in the anterior third, the widest part almost twice the narrowest part below the middle. Measurements (mm): head length to the lateral base of the mandible 1.17—1.35; head index 0.73; head—mandible index 0.50—0.70; postmentum waist width 0.22—0.25; pronotum length 0.40—0.47, width 0.75—0.84; pronotum index 0.55; antennae 14—15-segmented.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The holotype is an alate, the soldier and worker are morphotypes, in the National Museum of Victoria, Melbourne. Distribution: Victoria, New South Wales, Queensland and South Australia; North Island of New Zealand (introduced). This species nests strictly inside tree trunks, unlike C. acinaciformis, which builds domed mounds 1—2 feet high in arid scrub; it commonly damages telegraph poles, fence posts, building timber, fruit trees and vines, and also attacks living trees in the sclerophyll forests of Victoria and New South Wales.
